title: Measures to Mitigate Rising Temperatures and Create More Conducive Working and Living Environments
what_it_is: Measures to Mitigate Rising Temperatures and Create More Conducive Working and Living Environments

sections.label: Ambient temperature reduction trials
sections.summary: Past trials have shown a reduction of ambient temperatures by up to 2 degrees Celsius.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Past trials have shown a reduction of ambient temperatures by up to 2 degrees Celsius.

sections.label: Tree planting in industrial estates
sections.summary: Nearly 90,000 trees have been planted in industrial estates, with a goal to increase from 180,000 to about 260,000 trees by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: To date, nearly 90,000 trees have been planted in our industrial estates under the OneMillionTrees movement, with the help of our partners and the community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: These efforts have helped to beautify and cool industrial estates, such as Jurong Island, Seletar Aerospace Park and Tuas Industrial Estate, to create greener and more conducive workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We aim to increase the total number of trees across our industrial estates from 180,000 trees today, to about 260,000 trees by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Studies have shown that intensified tree planting in Singapore can reduce mid-day temperatures in the surrounding areas by up to 0.9 degrees Celsius.

sections.label: Three emissions scenarios
sections.summary: Three scenarios are described: business-as-usual, mitigating emissions, and continued use of fossil fuels for energy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: One is the business-as-usual scenario; the other is a scenario where we are taking good steps to mitigate emissions; and the third is to assume a situation where fossil fuels continue to be harnessed for energy.

sections.label: HDB Green Towns Programme
sections.summary: The HDB Green Towns Programme focuses on reducing energy consumption, recycling rainwater and cooling HDB towns, aiming to cut energy use by 15% from 2020 levels by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The HDB Green Towns Programme, which I mentioned, focuses on reducing energy consumption, recycling rainwater and cooling HDB towns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: We aim to reduce the energy consumption in HDB towns by 15% from 2020's level, by 2030.

sections.label: HDB building orientation and green cover
sections.summary: HDB buildings are oriented North-South and new estates require 45% to 60% green cover for a comfortable living environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: A specific example includes orienting the HDB buildings in the North-South direction and requiring 45% to 60% green cover in new estates to ensure sufficient greenery to create a comfortable living environment for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Double-glazed windows for HDB flats
sections.summary: Full glass windows in existing HDB flats admit heat, and a question asks whether HDB can install double-glazed windows for BTOs and existing flats under HIP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: For many of our existing HDB flats, we incorporate full glass windows that admit a considerable amount of heat during the late afternoon.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: So, my question is whether HDB can consider installing the low-heat transfer, double-glazed windows for BTOs moving forward, and also, as part of the features for existing HDB flats as part of the Home Improvement Programme (HIP)?

sections.label: Holistic climate planning across agencies
sections.summary: The Singapore Green Plan integrates multi-agency work, and inter-agency groups study heat effects on health and work practices.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Indeed, I think it is important for us to think about challenges very holistically.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And that is really the genesis of the Singapore Green Plan, which is to bring multi-agencies' work together and to integrate our plans, so that we are clear about the trajectory and pathway that we are heading towards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: Similarly, when we come to issues, such as how hotter temperatures are going to affect human health, there are also inter-agency work groups to study that, whether it is MOH with MSE on heat stress affecting human health, or MOH, MOM and the Workplace Safety and Health Council to study the impact of heat on our work practices.

sections.label: Climate research and inter-ministerial committee
sections.summary: Research studies climate change impacts on Singapore, and an Inter-Ministerial Committee chaired by Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean brings Ministries together to review policies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: It is really part of our research effort to understand various impacts of climate change on Singapore better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: And we also have the Inter-Ministerial Committee that is chaired by Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean that will bring the relevant Ministries together.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: As and when we are informed with new inputs, we will review the relevant policies and we will get the relevant Ministries together to study some of these cross-Ministry problems.

sections.label: Greenery and urban heat mitigation
sections.summary: NParks and Cooling Singapore 2.0 study greenery's impact on urban heat, finding large-canopy trees and denser planting improve outdoor thermal comfort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: For example, NParks is collaborating with researchers from the NRF-funded project, "Cooling Singapore 2.0", to study the impact of greenery on urban heat mitigation, specifically on tree shapes, planting configurations and size of green spaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: I am actually very heartened that the recent modelling study of trees in HDB residential precincts preliminarily shows that trees with large canopies, such as umbrella- and oblong-shaped trees, are more effective in improving outdoor thermal comfort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: In addition, increasing the tree planting densities, which we are doing under our OneMillionTrees movement, will lead to further improvements in outdoor thermal comfort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: And studies by other researchers have also shown that our structured multi-tiered planting – managed trees over shrubs, multi-layers of canopy – can reduce mid-day temperatures by up to 0.9 degrees Celsius.
